transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around. It's been going on for months now. 

Some days I just pick at a piece of toast and have a cup of coffee, and that's it. But then other days, I'll find myself standing in the bakery aisle at the store buying a bunch of sweets that I don't even really enjoy eating. It's just very all over the place.
After you have these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise. I just... I just eat it and then usually feel pretty bad about it later, but I don't try to get rid of it or undo it.
When you find yourself eating those large amounts of sweets, do you feel like you have lost control over your eating or that you are unable to stop once you have started?

No, not really. I don't feel like I've lost control or that I can't stop myself. I just... I decide to eat them, and I do. I could stop if I wanted to, I suppose. I don't feel out of control while it's happening, I just feel bad about it afterward.
Over the past two years, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless for most of the day, more days than not?

Yes, I have. For a long time now, most days I just wake up with this... this heavy, sad feeling just sitting on me. Even when I'm standing in my bright kitchen with the coffee going, I just feel like the warmth has gone out of everything. It's just there, most of the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or your ability to concentrate on daily tasks since this low mood began?

Yes, my energy has definitely changed. It's just... really low. Even after a full night of sleep, you know, on the nights when my aunt doesn't call out, I still feel completely worn down by breakfast time. I mean, just doing regular things... like carrying a basket of laundry or having to make a few phone calls, it just takes way more out of me than it should. It's hard to really focus on much when you feel that drained.
Are there things you used to enjoy doing that you no longer find any pleasure or interest in?

Yes, definitely. I used to really look forward to certain things. Like... I'd get excited about picking out new quilting squares, or going to bowling night, or even just helping plan the potlucks at church. But lately... I don't know. I look at my sewing supplies or I see the church calendar, and I just can't make myself care about it the way I used to. It's just flat.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches of two months or longer where you felt completely like your old self, without any of these sad or low-energy feelings?

No, not really. I mean, there might be a day or two here and there where I don't feel quite as heavy, but... no, I haven't had a stretch like that. It hasn't gone away for two whole months. It's just been pretty constant this whole time.
